Title: Birol et al. (2002) Penicillin production in a fed-batch fermentor (extended Bajpai and Reuss model)

Abstract: Simulation software based on a detailed unstructured model for penicillin production in a fed-batch fermentor has been developed. The model extends the mechanistic model of Bajpai and Reuss by adding input variables such as pH, temperature, aeration rate, agitation power, and feed flow rate of substrate and introducing the CO₂ evolution term. The simulation package was then used for monitoring and fault diagnosis of a typical penicillin fermentation process. The simulator developed may be used for both research and educational purposes and is available at the web site: http://www.chee.iit.edu/~control/software.html.

Laws:
(1) [balance] Biomass concentration balance with growth and dilution as culture volume changes.
(3) [constitutive] Specific biomass growth rate combining pH inhibition, Contois limitation by glucose and oxygen, and temperature-dependent growth and death.
(9) [balance] Penicillin concentration balance with non-growth-associated production, hydrolysis, and dilution as culture volume changes.
(10) [constitutive] Specific penicillin production rate as a function of glucose substrate inhibition and dissolved-oxygen limitation.
(11) [balance] Glucose concentration balance accounting for cellular consumption, substrate feed, and volume dilution.
(12) [balance] Dissolved-oxygen concentration balance with cellular uptake, oxygen transfer, and volume dilution.
(13) [constitutive] Correlation for the overall oxygen mass-transfer coefficient based on oxygen flow and agitation power per culture volume.
(14) [balance] Culture-volume balance accounting for substrate feed, acid/base addition, and evaporative loss.
(15) [constitutive] Temperature-dependent expression for the evaporative-loss rate from the culture volume.
(16) [constitutive] Heat-generation rate from biomass growth and biomass-associated maintenance activity.
(17) [balance] Temperature balance for a fed-batch fermentor with feed-temperature exchange, reaction heat, and cooling-coil heat removal.
(18) [constitutive] Carbon-dioxide evolution rate represented as contributions from biomass growth, maintenance, and penicillin production.

answer.description: This dynamic unstructured model describes penicillin production in a fed-batch fermentor and predicts biomass, penicillin, glucose, dissolved oxygen, culture volume, temperature, heat generation, and carbon dioxide. Extending the Bajpai–Reuss model, it combines growth and product-formation kinetics with glucose and oxygen consumption, oxygen transfer, volume change, heat effects, and carbon-dioxide evolution. The process is operated with adjustable substrate feed, aeration, and agitation; direct pH and temperature effects on penicillin production are not included.
